source_snapshot.procedure: Enable Platform First Error Handling, MCA threshold enable/count FFE and Reset After Sync-Flood; unlock CPU through HDT; boot Ubuntu 20.04, RHEL 9.0 or Windows 2022; install AMD RAS tool; list GMI links; then inject correctable errors at hardcoded link 0 for IOD location 0 and CCD location 1 with linktraffic 1 and errortype 0.
source_snapshot.criteria: Tool reports PASS and the OS reports within an unspecified timeout; inspect dmesg and the injection report against an unspecified AMD RAS specification.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; AMD RAS tool, HDT unlock and RAS hardware required; operator drives injection while the agent collects generic GMI/XGMI and SEL logs.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION/CHANGED; preserves two locations and adds owner gating, but does not resolve fixed link 0, timeout, Windows-versus-dmesg or deterministic per-location evidence.
source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 【During Test】 Hardware required: RDIMM with ECC / HDT Software tool: AMD RAS Error Injection Tool 1. BIOS settings: a. CPU Common Options → Platform First Error Handling: Enabled b. CPU Common Options → MCA error thresh enable: TRUE c. CPU Common Options → MCA error thresh count: FFE (Deviate from default setting FF5) d. FCH Common Options → FCH RAS Options → Reset After Sync-Flood: Enable 2. Unlock CPU via HDT. 3. Boot into Ubuntu 20.04/RHEL 9.0 / Windows 2022. 4. Download the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool, then install and open the software. 5. Enter the following commands: sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --listgmilinks 6. Run IOD Correctable Error Injection sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --gmixgmi --linknumber 0 --errorlocation 0 --linktraffic 1 --errortype 0 7. Run CCD Correctable Error Injection sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --gmixgmi --linknumber 0 --errorlocation 1 --linktraffic 1 --errortype 0 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria_direct_xlsx: 1. For Correctable errors, the tool provides a PASS status. 2. If the OS reports the error within a timeout period, the test passed. 3. If the OS does not report the error within a timeout period, the test failed. 4. Follow the AMD RAS Spec to check the dmesg and Error inject report.
source_snapshot.deepseek_direct_xlsx: PARTIAL | -- GMI3 Correctable Error: inject the GMI3 GMI3 Correctable Error via the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool (after HDT/unlock + the BIOS RAS knobs from the procedure, e.g. Platform First Error Handling=Enabled + per-unit MCA/UMC settings). Agent stages/verifies with sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg -T 2>&1 | tail -160 | grep -iE 'gmi|xgmi|link.error|corrected|uncorrected'; echo __GMI3_GMI3_Correctable_Error; ipmitool sel elist 2>&1 | tail -40 2>&1" but the tool injection step itself is interactive/HW-level and needs the user to drive the exact inject command.

test_case.test_name: GMI3 Correctable Error — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Verify correctable GMI3 handling independently at the approved IOD and CCD injection locations, proving that the selected physical link reports the expected corrected event within an authoritative interval and returns to healthy operation.
required_package: CPU/platform/GMI topology mapping from enumerated link identifiers to physical IOD and CCD resources
AMD RAS Error Injection Tool version/hash/license and exact AMD RAS specification revision
Approved meaning of linktraffic 1 and errortype 0 plus one-event/count behavior
Authoritative per-location timeout and corrected-event register/MCA/APEI/WHEA signature
Ubuntu/RHEL dmesg versus Windows WHEA evidence path and applicable BMC/UEFI expectations
BIOS FFE-versus-default-FF5 rationale, original values, HDT closeout, abort and recovery/restoration plan
test_case.test_command: Map every intended physical GMI link from `--listgmilinks`; preserve the exact BIOS/HDT/tool/CPU/firmware/OS baseline; obtain approval for CE flag semantics, IOD/CCD targets and one-event limits; inject one mapped IOD CE and one mapped CCD CE as separately controlled checkpoints; correlate each complete transcript with topology-specific MCA/APEI or Windows WHEA evidence, applicable BMC/UEFI records and link health; then close the injector and restore all BIOS/HDT state.
test_case.expected_result: 1. For Correctable errors, the tool provides a PASS status. 2. If the OS reports the error within a timeout period, the test passed. 3. If the OS does not report the error within a timeout period, the test failed. 4. Follow the AMD RAS Spec to check the dmesg and Error inject report.

safety_gate: Use an isolated non-production SUT with independent console, backup and recovery
Map the enumerated topology; never assume link 0 is the intended link on every platform
Preserve existing host and management logs rather than clearing away unrelated evidence
Inject only the approved single CE at one location at a time and stop on wrong target, UCE/fatal escalation, storm, reset, hang or link degradation
No automatic retry; close the injector and restore BIOS threshold, sync-flood and HDT state
expected_evidence: Tool/spec version/hash/license, `--listgmilinks` output and approved physical mapping
BIOS/HDT before, approved delta and restored values
Separate IOD and CCD command transcripts with parameters, timestamps, exit status and tool PASS
Per-location corrected MCA/APEI or WHEA signature within the approved timeout and applicable BMC/UEFI correlation
Stable link/device health, no UCE/fatal escalation, injector closeout, restoration and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: If the project intentionally qualifies only link 0, the platform recipe must document its physical IOD/CCD mapping and why other enumerated links are out of scope. Linux and Windows evidence must remain OS-specific rather than requiring dmesg universally.

source_conflict.reason: The source enumerates GMI links but then fixes both injections to link 0 without a mapping or coverage rule. Its timeout is undefined, and Windows 2022 is listed while Criteria requires dmesg. The Criteria also lacks distinct IOD-versus-CCD evidence, so a single generic corrected event could falsely satisfy both checkpoints.
